event.title: Advancing African Research in AI and Natural Language Processing
event.subtitle: Communicating African progress in AI and NLP research to the world's leading venues.
event.format: Talks, panels, oral sessions and interest groups
event.goal: Five African institutions accepted to top AI and NLP conference main tracks in 2027, with work led from Africa.
event.organiser: Victor A. Omolaoye (Hasso Plattner Institute), with LAUTECH
event.timezoneNote: Times are West Africa Time (WAT). Programme and speakers are provisional.

about.title: Artificial intelligence
about.text: Computer systems that recognise images, make predictions and reason. Most modern AI is machine learning: systems learn patterns from data rather than following hand-written rules.

about.title: Natural language processing
about.text: The branch of AI that works with human language: translation, speech recognition, search and large language models. Africa has more than 2,000 languages, and most have little digital data or tooling.

about.title: Where research is judged
about.text: New results appear mainly at peer-reviewed conferences: NeurIPS, ICML and ICLR for machine learning; ACL, EMNLP and NAACL for NLP. Main tracks typically accept around one in four or five submissions.

callForTalks.heading: PhD students: present your research
callForTalks.intro: Ten-minute talks in two sessions. Work in progress gets structured feedback from the room to strengthen it for ACL-family venues.

sessions.title: Session 1: Published work
sessions.text: Six 10-minute talks on accepted or published papers. Share what you found and what it took to get there.

sessions.title: Session 2: Work in progress
sessions.text: Five 10-minute talks on ongoing work with initial results, each followed by 5 minutes of audience feedback.
